summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of hepatic encephalopathy was admitted from rehab for worsening altered mental status, hallucinations, and anxiety. The confusion was multifactorial, attributed to a urinary tract infection and medication effects from oxycodone and Flexeril, with possible contribution from hepatic encephalopathy. She improved after discontinuation of sedating medications, treatment with ampicillin for UTI, and supportive care. Her chronic abdominal and back pain was managed without opioids using lubiprostone and acetaminophen. Neurological symptoms including intermittent facial droop and facial sensory changes persisted but were inconsistent with structural brain lesions, as prior and current imaging showed no acute abnormalities. She was discharged to extended care with instructions to avoid narcotics, complete her antibiotic course, and continue liver-directed therapy including lactulose and rifaximin, with ongoing transplant evaluation.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
